Magnesium Sulfate for Fetal Neuroprotection: Retreatment with magnesium sulfate in women at risk of preterm birth showed a potential reduction of 0 cases per 1,000 (ranging from 31 fewer to 38 more cases). The evidence quality was rated as high and deemed critical for decision-making. 2. Antibiotic Prophylaxis for Intact Membranes: The use of antibiotics in women at risk of preterm birth with intact membranes resulted in 5 more cases per 1,000 (ranging from 2 fewer to 14 more). The evidence quality was moderate and considered critical. 3. Antibiotic Prophylaxis for Ruptured Membranes: For women with preterm rupture of membranes, antibiotic prophylaxis showed a reduction of 5 cases per 1,000 (ranging from 17 fewer to 10 more). The evidence quality was moderate and critical. 4. Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC): Continuous KMC for preterm newborns reduced mortality by 40 cases per 1,000 (ranging from 5 fewer to 59 fewer). The evidence quality was moderate and critical. Intermittent KMC showed a reduction of 61 cases per 1,000 (ranging from 15 more to 119 fewer), with moderate evidence quality. 5. Plastic Bags or Wraps for Preterm Newborns: The use of plastic coverings immediately after birth in preterm newborns showed a reduction of 151 cases per 1,000 (ranging from 209 fewer to 345 more). The evidence quality was low and critical. 6. Early initiation of CPAP therapy for preterm newborns with respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) showed a reduction of 24 cases per 1,000 (ranging from 93 fewer to 135 more). The evidence quality was very low and critical. 7. Surfactant Replacement Therapy: Animal-derived surfactants for RDS showed a reduction of 18 cases per 1,000 (ranging from 59 fewer to 30 more). The evidence quality was low and critical. Protein-free synthetic surfactants showed a reduction of 13 cases per 1,000 (ranging from 1 fewer to 1 fewer). The evidence quality was low and critical. Protein-containing synthetic surfactants showed a reduction of 55 cases per 1,000 (ranging from 19 fewer to 80 fewer). The evidence quality was low and critical. 8. Prophylactic vs. Rescue Surfactant Therapy: Prophylactic surfactant therapy without CPAP showed a reduction of 31 cases per 1,000 (ranging from 8 fewer to 47 fewer). The evidence quality was low and critical. Prophylactic surfactant therapy with CPAP showed a reduction of 18 cases per 1,000 (ranging from 24 more to 50 fewer). The evidence quality was very low and critical. 9. Early vs. Late Surfactant Therapy: Early surfactant therapy (within 2–3 hours of birth) compared to late therapy (after symptoms worsen) showed a reduction of 16 cases per 1,000 (ranging from 34 fewer to 7 more). The evidence quality was very low and critical. 10. Radiant Warmers vs. Incubators: The use of radiant warmers for unstable or sick preterm newborns showed an increase of 21 cases per 1,000. The evidence quality was very low and considered important. 11. Plastic Bags or Wraps for Preterm Newborns: The use of plastic coverings immediately after birth in preterm newborns showed a reduction of 151 cases per 1,000 (ranging from 209 fewer to 345 more). The evidence quality was low and critical. 12. Mode of Delivery for Preterm Birth: The comparison between cesarean section and vaginal delivery for preterm births in singleton pregnancies showed no pooled data due to very low evidence quality. 13. Antibiotic Regimens for Ruptured Membranes: A comparison of 3-day versus 7-day ampicillin regimens showed a reduction of 21 cases per 1,000 (ranging from 30 fewer to 65 more). The evidence quality was low and critical. 14. Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) vs. Conventional Care: Continuous KMC reduced mortality by 40 cases per 1,000 (ranging from 5 fewer to 59 fewer). The evidence quality was moderate and critical. 15. Surfactant Therapy Timing: Early surfactant therapy (within 2–3 hours of birth) compared to late therapy (after symptoms worsen) showed a reduction of 16 cases per 1,000 (ranging from 34 fewer to 7 more). The evidence quality was very low and critical. These findings highlight the importance of evidence-based interventions to improve outcomes for preterm births, with varying levels of evidence quality and criticality.
